findings.evidence: Peetre.lean:182 states the same conclusion from `‖x‖ = c * ‖y‖`, which implies both hypotheses of the new lemma, since `‖y‖ ≤ c‖y‖ = ‖x‖ ≤ c‖x‖` when `c ≥ 1`. The only use of the old lemma is at Peetre.lean:240.
findings.fix: Make the old lemma a corollary of the new one: `one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_of_norm_le_mul hc s h.le (by rw [h]; nlinarith [norm_nonneg y])`. Alternatively, delete it and rewrite its single use (`one_add_norm_smul_sq_rpow_le`, line 240) to call the new lemma.
findings.issue: `one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_of_norm_le_mul` generalizes the existing `one_add_norm_sq_rpow_le_of_norm_eq_mul` (line 182), yet the old lemma keeps its own near-clone proof (the same two-case split on the sign of `s`, the same `Real.rpow_le_rpow` / `rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos` steps). findings.evidence: HomogeneousSymbol.lean:431 `def compPosition ... coefficient p := a.coefficient (g p.1, p.2)`. Pullback.lean:439 `compPosition_eq_pullback`. Each `*_pullback` lemma at Pullback.lean:445-476 mirrors a `*_compPosition` lemma at HomogeneousSymbol.lean:449-476, and both sets are proved by `rfl`.
findings.fix: Keep one construction. Either define `compPosition a g hg := a.pullback g (fun _ ↦ .id ℝ E) hg contDiff_const _` and derive its lemmas from the `pullback` ones, or replace `compPosition` and its uses with `pullback` at `L = id`, removing the duplicate lemma family.
findings.issue: `HomogeneousSymbol.pullback g L` contains the existing `HomogeneousSymbol.compPosition g` as its `L = id` case (the PR's own `compPosition_eq_pullback`). The PR nevertheless adds a second simp API (`zero_/add_/neg_/sub_/smul_/comp_pullback`) that restates `zero_/add_/neg_/sub_/smul_/comp_compPosition` (HomogeneousSymbol.lean:449-476) one by one.

summary: The PR's symbol-level pullback is new, but it adds two parallel APIs next to existing ones: a Japanese-bracket comparison lemma that re-proves an existing special case with the same proof, and a homogeneous-symbol pullback whose identity-family case is the existing `compPosition` API with its own simp set.
